newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK war victims fight for reparation from Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: HK war victims fight for reparation from Tokyo.

text.p: Elderly Hong Kong war victims protested in front of government headquarters on Tuesday, urging the colonial administration to press Japan to compensate them for hardships suffered during World War Two.
Holding placards and chanting slogans, the group of about 12 people said Britain would be irresponsibile if it did not help them fight for compensation.
"The British must clear this mess up before they go," cried Ng Yat-hing of the Reparation Association Hong Kong.
Japan occupied Hong Kong from late 1941 to late 1945 during Britain's rule in the territory. Britain ends 156 years of colonial rule of Hong Kong at midnight June 30.
Ng, 65, said his group had 3,400 member-families who held a total of 540 million Japanese military currency notes which they were forced to buy with Hong Kong notes during the occupation.
"These are all useless and Japan must pay," Ng said.
Ng said the group filed a lawsuit at a Tokyo district court in 1993. Officials at the Japanese consulate in Hong Kong would not comment on the court case.
